title: Data Quality & Freshness Maintenance
purpose: Keep stored data accurate, fresh, and well-organized over time. Defines periodic health checks, freshness rules, tag hygiene, deduplication, and index rebuild protocols to prevent knowledge base decay.

periodic_health_checks.title: Periodic Health Checks
periodic_health_checks.overview: Run automated checks on a regular cadence to detect staleness, structural issues, and disconnected entries before they accumulate.

steps.action: Run staleness_detector.py weekly to identify entries that may be outdated
steps.output: List of entries with staleness scores and recommended actions (review, refresh, or archive)

steps.action: Run fast_validate on all indexes to check structural integrity
steps.expected: All indexes pass validation. Any failures should be fixed immediately before other maintenance.

steps.action: Run graph_query.py --orphans to find disconnected entries
steps.expected: Zero orphans. Any orphans found should be connected via builds_on references or flagged for review.
steps.remediation: For each orphan, search for related entries and add appropriate builds_on links. If no related entries exist, the orphan may be a candidate for deletion or may need companion entries.

steps.action: Run handoff_tracker.py to find unresolved items from previous team sessions
steps.expected: All handoff items are either resolved or assigned to active teams. Stale unresolved items older than 2 weeks should be escalated.

freshness_rules.title: Freshness Rules
freshness_rules.overview: Define age-based thresholds for different content types. Stale content degrades trust in the knowledge base.

rules.action: Flag for review. The original research question should be re-evaluated: is the answer still accurate? Have new sources emerged?
review_process: Check if the primary sources cited are still accessible
Search for newer sources on the same topic
If findings still hold, update the last_reviewed date
If findings are outdated, trigger SOP-023 for a fresh research cycle

rules.action: Verify URLs still respond and API contracts have not changed
review_process: Send a test request to each documented endpoint
Verify response format matches the documented schema
Check for deprecation notices in API documentation
Update rate limits and authentication requirements if changed

rules.trigger: Underlying tool or system has been updated since the benchmark was recorded
rules.action: Re-run benchmarks using the same methodology
review_process: Check if the benchmarked tool version matches the currently installed version
If versions differ, re-run the benchmark
Record new results alongside old results for trend analysis
Update the entry with new data and set builds_on to the previous benchmark entry

tag_hygiene.title: Tag Hygiene
tag_hygiene.overview: Maintain a clean, consistent tag system. Poor tag hygiene makes search unreliable and creates organizational debt.

steps.action: List all tags and their usage counts monthly

rules: If the tag represents a valid concept: find or create sibling entries that should share the tag
If the tag is too specific: merge it into a broader canonical tag and update taxonomy.json
If the tag was a mistake: remove it from the entry and taxonomy.json
steps.goal: No canonical tag should have fewer than 2 entries unless it was recently created

rules: Consider splitting into more specific sub-tags
Add the new sub-tags to taxonomy.json with the broad tag listed in aliases for backwards compatibility
Re-tag affected entries with the more specific sub-tags
Update the consolidations map in taxonomy.json

steps.action: Enforce new tag policy: all tags must exist in taxonomy.json before use
steps.gate: kb_validator.py rejects entries with tags not found in taxonomy.json canonical names
process_for_new_tags: Propose the new tag with name, namespace, description, and aliases
Verify it does not overlap with an existing tag (check aliases and consolidations)
Add to taxonomy.json tags array and consolidations map
Then use the tag in the entry

deduplication.title: Deduplication
deduplication.overview: Detect and merge entries with high content overlap to prevent knowledge base bloat and contradictory information.

steps.action: Run cross_ref_checker.py to find entries with 90%+ content similarity
steps.output: List of entry pairs with similarity scores above the threshold

steps.action: For each duplicate pair, determine which entry to keep
criteria: Keep the more complete entry (more content, more references, more tags)
If roughly equal, keep the more recent entry
If one entry is referenced by more builds_on links, prefer keeping that one to minimize cascading updates

steps.action: Merge the duplicate into the kept entry
process: Copy any unique information from the removed entry into the kept entry
Merge tag sets (union of both entries' tags)
Update builds_on: the kept entry inherits all builds_on references from the removed entry
Find all entries that reference the removed entry in their builds_on and update them to point to the kept entry

commands: Remove the deleted entry from knowledge-base/index.json
Update all builds_on references across the knowledge base
Run fast_validate to confirm structural integrity

index_rebuild_protocol.title: Index Rebuild Protocol
index_rebuild_protocol.overview: After any batch of changes, rebuild indexes in the correct order to ensure consistency.

steps.action: After any batch of KB changes, rebuild the unified search index
steps.when: After adding, removing, or modifying any knowledge base entries

steps.action: After any KB changes, run validators
steps.rule: Do not consider the changes complete until both validators pass

steps.action: After any relationship changes, regenerate the relationship graph
steps.when: After modifying builds_on references, adding or removing entries, or merging duplicates
steps.verification: Run graph_query.py --stats to confirm node and edge counts are as expected

ordering_rules: Always rebuild indexes BEFORE running validators
Always regenerate the relationship graph AFTER index rebuild
If validators fail, fix the issue and re-run the full rebuild sequence
Never skip validators even if the change seems trivial

weekly_health_check: Run staleness_detector.py and review flagged entries
Run graph_query.py --orphans and resolve any orphans
Run handoff_tracker.py and escalate stale unresolved items
monthly_maintenance: Run unified_search.py --list-tags and review tag distribution
quarterly_maintenance: Review all research entries older than 90 days
Verify all API source URLs still respond
Re-run benchmarks for any tools that have been updated
Full index rebuild and validation sweep
